# PARA AI solution

This repo coordinates multiple Copilot CLI sessions through JSON files in `data/` (git-ignored) and a .NET bridge.

- Every named/custom/default Copilot CLI session, including unknown and unassigned sessions, MUST follow the `para-session-protocol` skill. Keep only your own `data/sessions/<sessionId>.json` current.
- Before material analysis, delegation or coding on every new task, record `estimate: {points, rationale}`. Points measure relative complexity/uncertainty, never elapsed-time promises. Approved independent CLI work executes directly without a Bridge grant. Larger work is broken into bounded units; Bridge orchestration is opt-in for explicitly delegated work, not a prerequisite for ordinary CLI work.
- Analyze every new task and ask human implementation approval; smallness is NOT an approval exemption. Inherited bounded approval does not authorize scope expansion. Never automatically open a PR, push, merge or close an external source item.
- New orchestration uses your append-only `outbox` (request/report/cancel), not scalar `handoff` replacement. The Bridge owns the sole canonical assignment list (`data/bridge/state.json`, Protocol 2, `Delegations`), receipts and inbox execution. Agents estimate and judge; deterministic code grants ownership, schedules and delivers.
- Sessions NEVER write another session's file, `data/bridge/` or `data/inbox/` (including scrum-master). Shared ledger/inbox reads are read-only. Do not recruit discovered/unassigned sessions automatically; they participate through their own requests.
- Do not submit new `mode: self` requests: an attended CLI cannot be automatically resumed. Use `mode: new` for autonomous Bridge-managed work. Existing ungranted self requests reserve nothing; their creator cancels them before continuing directly or submitting a new managed request. Never bypass an existing running/uncertain assignment, write another session's state, or invent a grant. Bridge-assigned workers still require their owned running grant.
- Read-only managed requests explicitly use `accessMode: read_only`, `reads: ["relative/path"]`, `writes: []`. Empty/missing reads means whole-repository read scope. Omitting accessMode preserves legacy behavior: `writes: []` is exclusive, NOT read-only. Readers can coexist; overlapping readers/writers cannot. Never amend old emitted commands to change scopes.
- A supervisor publishes sibling requests once, then sets `waiting_input` with an AI need/question and YIELDS. Durable reports wake Bridge-managed supervisors; human needs pause automatic resumption. Only explicit `done`/`failed` assignment reports are terminal: a returned chat, session `result` or `waiting_input` is not assignment completion.
- Never commit `.env` or anything under `data/`.
- Task-specific scripts and review artifacts stay outside the repo (on the user's Windows machine: `C:/Users/727124/src/prompts`). The reusable, cross-machine Playwright/video helper explicitly requested for this repo lives in `tools/review-media`; generated media and secrets never do.
- Use agents in `.github/agents` for role focus (`coordinator`, `coder`, `researcher`, `reviewer`, `scrum-master`, `functional-reviewer`, `hr`); new delegation uses self-contained outbox requests, never assumed shared context. Existing legacy handoffs remain supported for recovery only.
